title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks - Standards & Playbook
author: Ari Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and runbook structure. It is intended as the canonical guidance for service owners and SREs responsible for production reliability.

Goals
- Provide consistent, measurable SLOs across Redwood services
- Standardize error budget policy and automation for fast, objective decisions
- Ensure capacity planning aligns with business commitments and predictable SLAs
- Make incident reviews actionable and blameless, with clear follow-up
- Maintain runbooks that are concise, tested, and accessible to on-call engineers
- Use a small, well-integrated operational toolset for monitoring, tracing, and alerting

Scope and Ownership
- Scope: HTTP/GRPC inference endpoints (hosted API), serving runtime, routing layer, dedicated capacity control plane, and supporting infra (ingress, auth, billing hooks).
- Service Owner: product / service-specific owner listed in service metadata.
- Reliability Owner: SRE on-call rotation assigned to the service.
- Review Cadence: SLO review every quarter and when a major product change is planned.

1) SLO Definitions and Examples
- All SLOs must be defined in terms of measurable signals (Prometheus, BigQuery, or metrics sent to central telemetry).
- Each SLO doc must include: SLI definition, measurement window, target, measurement owner, and automation for error budget spend tracking.

Canonical SLOs (examples)
| Service Area | SLI | Target (rolling 30d) | Alerting Burn Rule | Owner |
|--------------|-----|---------------------:|-------------------:|-------|
| Text generation API (public) | Availability (5xx rate on production route) | 99.95% | Page if burn > 5%/day | api-team@redwood.com |
| Low-latency inference path (prod) | P99 latency (inference only) | < 600ms | Alert if p99 > 1s for 30m | serving-runtime@redwood.com |
| Embeddings API | Successful responses within timeout | 99.9% | Alert if > 1% errors sustained 1h | embeddings-team@redwood.com |

Notes:
- Measurement window: 30-day rolling by default. Teams may add a 7-day short-window for fast detection but official error budget accounting uses 30d.
- Availability SLI should exclude planned maintenance windows documented in the calendar and flagged with a maintenance metric.

2) Error Budget Policy and Automation
- Error budget defined as 1 - SLO (e.g., for 99.95% SLO monthly error budget = 0.05% of requests).
- Automated burn tracking: central error-budget service evaluates SLIs daily and publishes current burn rate to the SRE dashboard and to the #sre-error-budget Slack channel.
- Burn thresholds and action:
  1. Healthy: burn <= 25% of monthly budget - normal operations.
  2. Elevated: burn > 25% && <= 50% - engineering leads notified; postpone non-essential launches.
  3. High: burn > 50% && <= 100% - require meeting with SRE and product manager to review mitigations; pause non-critical rollouts.
  4. Exhausted: burn > 100% - on-call escalation to oncall-ops; require immediate mitigation and rollback if rollouts contributed.
- Automated actions: feature-flag gates can be configured to automatically disable experimental routes when burn > 75% (opt-in per-service).

3) Capacity Planning (Quarterly + Event-driven)
- Inputs: historical QPS, 95/99th percentile token length, batching efficiency metrics, KV cache hit rates, scheduled marketing events, sales bookings (enterprise contracts).
- Planning cadence:
  - Quarterly capacity review (SRE + product + infra): update demand forecast and purchase schedule.
  - Event-driven review: any major launch (>=10% expected QPS increase) triggers a 30/14/7/0 day readiness checklist.

Capacity planning checklist (condensed)
1. Verify forecast inputs and assumptions (owner: product).
2. Translate QPS to GPU-hours using current production perf profile (owner: serving-runtime).
3. Confirm physical/virtual capacity availability (owner: infra).
4. Reserve Dedicated or autoscaling policies as needed (owner: infra/sales-ops).
5. Run soak tests at 1.2x expected peak for 2 hours (owner: SRE test harness).
6. Validate end-to-end SLOs during soak (owner: SRE).

Capacity formulas (examples)
- Required GPUs = ceil((peak_QPS * avg_tokens_per_request * cost_per_token_seconds) / gpu_token_throughput)
- Batching efficiency: effective_tokens = peak_QPS * avg_tokens_per_request * batching_multiplier (measure from load tests)

4) Reliability Initiatives and Roadmap Alignment
- Reliability initiatives must be prioritized in the quarterly roadmap if they impact customer-facing SLAs or error budgets.
- Initiative examples: improved KV cache eviction, shard-aware routing, p99 kernel optimization, autoscaler tuning.
- Initiative template (one-pager): problem statement, customer impact, hypothesis, success metrics (SLI improvement, cost delta), rollout plan, rollback plan, owners.

5) Incident Review Standards (Postmortem expectations)
- All Sev2/Sev1 incidents require a postmortem within 72 hours and a public summary in the incident channel within 8 hours.
- Postmortem structure (required sections):
  1. Summary (1-2 sentences)
  2. Impact (customers, SLOs breached, duration)
  3. Timeline (UTC times with actor/actions)
  4. Root cause analysis (technical cause and latent conditions)
  5. Corrective actions (with owners and due dates)
  6. Preventative actions (instrumentation, runbook updates, architecture changes)
  7. Follow-up status (open/closed)
- Action tracking: all corrective actions must have an owner and a due date. SRE manager does a 30/60/90-day audit for high-severity incidents.

6) Operational Tooling (standard stack)
- Monitoring: Prometheus + Cortex (central metrics), with standardized metric names and labels.
- Visualization & Dashboards: Grafana (team dashboards + central SRE dashboards).
- Tracing: Jaeger/Tempo with service and request id propagation across the control plane and runtime.
- Logging: Structured logs to ELK stack / BigQuery for long-term analytics.
- Alerts: Alertmanager with routing rules to on-call; critical alerts page with runbook link.
- Incident comms: Slack incident channels, Statuspage for public incidents.
- Automation: central error-budget service, automatic canary analysis pipeline (Argo Rollouts / homegrown runner).

Operational tooling requirements
- Every service must export standard labels: service_name, environment, cluster, zone, build_sha.
- SLIs must be exported as a time series with labels (slo_name, window="30d").
- Dashboards must have a 1-click link to the primary runbook.

7) Runbook Standards and Template
- Runbooks must be: concise (<= 2 pages when printed), executable, verified annually, and owned.
- Format requirements:
  - Title: Service + primary symptom (e.g., "Text-gen: High 5xx Rate")
  - Symptoms: quick bullet list of signals that indicate the problem
  - Immediate mitigations (ordered steps) - actionable CLI or console commands where possible
  - Diagnostics (what to check & how)
  - Escalation path (who to call, Slack channels, on-call rotation link)
  - Post-incident steps and pointers to postmortem template

Runbook example (abbreviated)
- Title: Text-Gen - High 5xx Rate
- Symptoms:
  - Production 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes
  - Error budget burn > 10%/day
- Immediate mitigations (ordered):
  1. Confirm metric: grafana -> "textgen.http.errors" (last 10m)
  2. If > 1% and p99 latency also high: set routing weight to fallback model (CLI: redwoodctl route set-weight --service textgen --variant model-fallback --weight 80)
  3. If errors from a specific region: disable region in routing policy (redwoodctl routing disable-region --region eu-west-1)
  4. If caused by model version: rollback to previous stable model (rollout ID in release notes)
- Diagnostics:
  - Check pod/container logs for OOMs or kernel errors: kubectl logs -n prod svc-textgen -l version=<version> --since=15m
  - Check GPU utilization and memory: node-exporter and nvidia-smi dashboards
  - Trace a sample failing request with trace id from logs
- Escalation:
  - If mitigations fail after 15 minutes, page SRE lead and product manager. Use channel #inc-textgen for comms.

8) Testing and Validation of Runbooks
- Runbooks must be exercised during game days at least once per quarter for each high-impact service.
- Game day checklist: inject failure, verify runbook steps, time-to-mitigation, and update runbook based on friction points.

9) Documentation and Metadata Requirements
- Every service Confluence page must include a reliability section with: SLOs, current error budget status link, runbook link, on-call rotation, and quarterly capacity forecast.
- Metadata fields to maintain in service registry (simple key/value): service_name, owner_email, reliability_owner_email, primary_runbook_url, slo_document_url, current_budget_percent_remaining.

10) Governance and Review
- SRE leadership runs a biweekly review of services with >50% error budget burn or repeated incidents.
- Any change to an SLO or measurement must go through a change control note (template) and be approved by SRE lead and product manager.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Links
- Error budget dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/error-budgets
- SLO policy repo (automation): git@github.com:redwood/sre-error-budget.git
- Canary analysis: https://argo-rollouts.internal.redwood.com
- Example rollout rollback command: redwoodctl rollout rollback --service textgen --to revision-20260214
- Postmortem template: /confluence/templates/postmortem-template

Change log

- 2026-03-04: Minor clarifications to burn thresholds and runbook template (reviewers: M. Patel, J. Lee)

Contact and escalation
- SRE Pager: oncall@sre.redwood.com
- SRE Ops Slack: #sre-ops
- Reliability Leadership: reliability-leads@redwood.com

This document is intended to be referenced by service owners and SREs when authoring SLOs, running capacity planning, conducting incident reviews, and authoring operational runbooks. For questions or suggestions, open a PR against this page or contact the SRE lead.
